title: MIN and MAX: fastest and slowest

screens.prompt: In B6, return the fastest of the four lap times in B2:B5 with MIN.

hints.syntax: Start with = and close the bracket: =MIN(B2:B5).
hints.func-min: The fastest lap is the smallest number in the column. MIN finds it; AVERAGE answers 60.65, which is not a lap anybody ran.
hints.require-ref: Point MIN at B2:B5. Lap times typed into the formula freeze at today's numbers and stop moving when a lap is re-run.
hints.value: That is not the fastest lap. A range that stops early or starts late hides the runner who was quicker.
hints.error: #VALUE! appears when a word is passed straight in, as =MIN("Fastest"). Labels sitting inside a range are skipped without complaint.

screens.prompt: In B6, return the slowest of the four lap times in B2:B5 with MAX.

hints.syntax: Start with = and close the bracket: =MAX(B2:B5).
hints.func-max: The slowest lap is the largest number in the column. MAX finds it; MIN answers the other end of the same four laps.
hints.require-ref: Point MAX at B2:B5, because a slowest time typed in stops updating the moment the race is re-run.
hints.value: That is not the slowest lap. A range that stops early leaves out the runner who took longest.
hints.error: MAX returns #REF! when the range points at cells that have been deleted. Check that the reference still covers B2:B5.

docs.syntax: =MIN(number1, ...) for the smallest, =MAX(number1, ...) for the largest
docs.explain:
MIN returns the smallest number in a range and MAX the largest. The four laps are 61.2 in B2, 58.4 in B3, 63.9 in B4 and 59.1 in B5, so MIN over B2:B5 gives Ben's 58.4 and MAX gives Cai's 63.9. Neither function sorts the sheet or cares which row a time sits in.

This exercise asks for the fastest lap on one screen and the slowest on the other. Fastest is the smallest number, so both answers come from the same four cells with the function swapped. The average of the four is 60.65, a time nobody ran, and it answers neither question.

Point both formulas at B2:B5 instead of typing the four times. A re-run lap then changes the answer, and a range that stops a row early hides the runner who was quicker.

errors.text: A word was passed as an argument in its own right, as in =MIN(Fastest), so there is no number to compare.
The range names cells that were deleted with their rows or their sheet, so MIN has nothing left to read.
One cell inside the range already holds that error, and MIN passes it back instead of the fastest lap.

docs.atWork: Race results and delivery logs, where the question is who came first or last, and the average never answers it.
docs.outcome: Return the smallest or largest number in a range without sorting the sheet first.

seo.title: MIN and MAX in Excel: fastest and slowest
seo.description: Four lap times, 61.2, 58.4, 63.9 and 59.1. MIN answers 58.4 and MAX answers 63.9 without sorting the sheet, while the average of 60.65 belongs to nobody.
